text: When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to take possession of it, and drives out before you many nations—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, seven nations more numerous and stronger than you—
and when the LORD your God gives them over to you and you defeat them, then you must devote them to destruction. Make no covenant with them and show them no mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughter to their son or take their daughter for your son,
for they would turn your son away from following me to serve other gods, and the LORD's anger would burn against you and destroy you quickly.
Instead, this is what you are to do to them: tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their idols in the fire.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his people, his treasured possession.
It was not because you were more numerous than other peoples that the LORD set his heart on you and chose you—you were the fewest of all peoples.

It was because the LORD loved you and kept the oath he swore to your fathers that he brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the house of slavery, from the hand of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Know therefore that the LORD your God is God, the faithful God, who keeps his covenant of steadfast love to a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commandments,
but who repays to their face those who hate him, destroying them. He does not delay; he repays to their face those who hate him.
So keep the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances that I am commanding you today, and do them.
And because you listen to these ordinances and keep them and do them, the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant of steadfast love that he swore to your fathers.

He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land—your grain, your new wine, and your oil—the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks, in the land he swore to your fathers to give you.
You will be blessed above all peoples. No man or woman among you will be barren, nor any of your livestock.

versions.text: You will be blessed above all peoples. No man or woman among you will be childless, nor any of your livestock barren.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew uses one word pair (עָקָר וַעֲקָרָה, "sterile male and barren female") for both people and animals; translating it "childless" for people and "barren" for animals splits a single idea and weakens the parallel.

text: The LORD will keep every sickness away from you, and none of the terrible diseases of Egypt that you knew will he inflict on you; he will lay them on all who hate you.
You will consume all the peoples the LORD your God gives over to you. Show them no pity, and do not serve their gods, for that would be a snare to you.
If you say in your heart, "These nations are more numerous than I am; how can I drive them out?"—

versions.text: If you say in your heart, "These nations are greater than I am; how can I drive them out?"—
versions.explanation: רַבִּים here means "many/more numerous," as rendered in verse 1 ("more numerous and stronger than you"). "Greater" is vaguer and loses the link with verse 1, where the same concern about numbers is raised.

text: do not be afraid of them. Remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

the great trials your own eyes saw, the signs and wonders, the mighty hand and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you fear.
The LORD your God will also send hornets among them, until even the survivors who hide from you have perished.
Do not be terrified of them, for the LORD your God is in your midst, a great and awesome God.
The LORD your God will drive out those nations before you little by little. You cannot finish them off quickly, or the wild animals would multiply against you.

versions.text: The LORD your God will drive out those nations before you little by little. You cannot finish them off all at once, or the wild animals would multiply against you.
versions.explanation: מַהֵר means "quickly, swiftly," contrasting with "little by little." "All at once" shifts the sense from speed to simultaneity.

text: But the LORD your God will give them over to you and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.
Burn the images of their gods in the fire. Do not covet the silver and gold on them or take it for yourself, or you will be ensnared by it, for it is detestable to the LORD your God.
Do not bring any detestable thing into your house, or you, like it, will be devoted to destruction. Utterly detest it and abhor it, for it is devoted to destruction.

versions.text: Do not bring any detestable thing into your house, or you, like it, will be devoted to destruction. Utterly detest it and abhor it, for it is set apart for destruction.
versions.explanation: The same word חֵרֶם occurs twice in this verse; rendering it two different ways ("devoted to destruction" / "set apart for destruction") obscures the deliberate repetition that gives the verse its force when read aloud.
